How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the
following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to
the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person
per item. At the Chair’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to
address the Community Services Commission.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting day will
be forwarded to the Commission before the meeting for their consideration but will not be
read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to
Commission but may not be received before the meeting.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

   MINUTES OF JULY 1, 2024
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Duong called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at 6:31
P.M. on Monday, July 1, 2024, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber at City Hall,
425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Lotz

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Nancy Duong, Justin Lotz, Darwin Rodriguez

Commissioners Absent:  Davis Barrantes, Ting Xie

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Assistant Director Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit
comments and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services
Commission, email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  None.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  JULY 1, 2024
 3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Lotz, seconded by Commissioner Rodriguez, to
  approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for June 3, 2024.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 3-0-0-2 as follows:

  AYES:  DUONG, LOTZ, RODRIGUEZ
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  BARRANTES, XIE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT COMMUNICATIONS PLAN
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  Commissioners discussed updates on cancellations and inquired about a triage
  communication system for urgent weekend issues. The commission was impressed by
  the bi-weekly newsletters' open and click rates, raised questions about consent, and
  suggested boosting text messages in multiple languages.

  The commission supports using text messages for cancellations and updates and
  prefers receiving information via email, website, and text. They talked about automated
  systems and hope to encourage similar systems across the city and departments.

  Public Comment: None

  B. EVENTS AND PROGRAM UPDATES
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  The Commission inquired whether attendees might be turned away at the
  Independence Day Event due to capacity. They also noted that the registration process
  for July 3rd was very straightforward. Additionally, the Commission raised questions
  regarding registration and the number of tickets available. They also expressed a desire
  to see increased attendance, given the city's significant investment in this program.

  Public Comment: None

  C. DISCUSSION OF 2024 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Presented by Chair Duong.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  JULY 1, 2024
   The Commission requested to review the RFP for the new registration software. They
  also agreed to cancel the August meeting, given that the City Council meeting is also
  canceled that day. Additionally, the September meeting will be canceled due to Labor
  Day.

  The Commission talked about the Youth Ambassador Program and the scheduling of
  interviews. They plan to hold a special meeting in September for the interviews.

5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

  Commissioner Lotz addressed playground safety and proposed monthly inspections
  for playgrounds that feature wood chips, specifically mentioning Smith Park. He also
  expressed concerns regarding the safety of playgrounds located at schools.

  Commissioner Rodriguez visited Washington School Park and voiced his concerns
  regarding safety. He observed the presence of dogs, despite signs indicating that they
  are now allowed.

  Chair Duong attended movie night and noted a decline in attendance. Nevertheless,
  she found the event enjoyable and witnessed community members dancing along to
  the music.

6. STAFF COMMENTS

  None.

7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Duong adjourned the meeting at 7:51 p.m.

  The next regular meeting held on Monday, October 7, 2024, in the Council Chamber at
  City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, at 6:30 pm.

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  October 7, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Ana Casillas, Recreation Supervisor
  Jackie Villalvazo, Recreation Coordinator

SUBJECT:  Summer Youth Programming Recap

Summer Camp
The Community Services Department held the popular Summer Camp program from June
10 through August 16. The camp for youth, ages 5- 12 ran from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
and was held at Coolidge Elementary School for Weeks 1-9 and the San Gabriel Scout
House/Mission Playhouse Glassroom for Week 10. The camp which had approximately
100 campers each week, with the exception of week 10. The program included themed
weeks featuring arts & crafts, weekly swim day, structured games, field trips, and spirit
days. A few highlights from the camp were the STEAM activities such as building a
volcano, field trip to John’s Incredible Pizza, with hands-on pizza making, and an in-house
Mad Science show. Next summer, staff plan to incorporate even more hands-on STEAM
activities.

Summer Parks With A Mission
The Summer Parks with A Mission free program was offered to youth ages 5-12 years old
and held at McKinley Elementary school. The program consisted of two sessions, the first
session was held from June 12- July 10 for McKinley students only and had 36 participants
enrolled. Session two was held from July 11-August 2, was open to all students and had
full registration with 45 participants enrolled. The program included themed weeks, crafts,
board games, sports activities. A couple highlights of the program were a create your own
puppet show event and pet rock habitat activity.

Jefferson Sports Academy
Jefferson Sports Academy was hosted from June 12- July 10. Enrollment grew to 59
students this summer. Sports staff focused on three sports: Soccer, Basketball and
Volleyball and taught participants the basics of each sport, built techniques, and held
practice games. The focus of the program was to build a good foundation, enhance a
passion for the sport, and prepare them for tryouts when the school year began. In
 addition to hands-on sports time, the program also offered one activity/craft per week
and ended with a celebratory pizza party.

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  October 7, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Andy Shoup, Recreation Supervisor
  Danielle Adriano, Recreation Coordinator

SUBJECT:  Summer in San Gabriel Series and Swim Classes Update

Summer in San Gabriel Series
The City of San Gabriel kicked of the Summer in San Gabriel Series with the inaugural
Culture Fest Event. This took place in the historic Mission District on Thursday, June 13.
Residents and visitors alike enjoyed captivating cultural performances and live music
presented by The Music Center. In addition, participants enjoyed delectable cuisines from
the Blossom Market Hall and an assortment of food trucks, engaging arts and crafts for
children, and community organization booths which provided a variety of family-friendly
activities. This special event reflected San Gabriel’s dedication to offering the community
enriching and entertaining experiences.

The series continued with three Movie and Concert evenings at Vincent Lugo Park and
two concerts at the Mission Playhouse Plaza. Residents enjoyed the summer nights with
live musical guests, movies, food trucks, fresh popcorn, and community organization
booths. One evening was specifically marketed as a “Kids Concert,” which featured a duo
of Kid’s Magicians and Sing Along Songs, Mario themed crafts, and the Super Mario Movie
concluded the evening.

Learn to Swim Classes
Learn to Swim Classes were taught by Certified Water Safety Instructors from June 10 –
August 16 at Smith Park Pool. Facing significant staffing challenges, the lesson schedule
was redesigned to maximize both attendance and effective instructor coverage. Despite
the challenges, the Aquatic Staff were able to offer a full slate of classes, with most levels
reaching their maximum capacities. As more instructors were trained, additional classes
were offered, and quickly taken, by our residents. A total of 475 registrations were taken
for swim classes.
 In preparation for Summer 2025, a strong emphasis will be placed on early recruitment
efforts and in-house training and certification courses. The goal is a fully staffed aquatics
team that will enable the City to grow the available spaces in the Learn to Swim Program,
as well as offerings of Public Swimming, Junior Lifeguard Course, Lap Swimming, and
Special Events.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  April 1, 2024

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  2024 Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Community Services Commission and is
intended for the 2024 calendar year. The Community Services Commission approved the
2023 Workplan on December 5, 2022, which was originally carried over from the 2022
Annual Workplan. The 2022 Annual Workplan was approved by the City Council during
the September 6, 2022 City Council meeting. The draft for 2024 outlined in this report
includes items from the 2023 workplan and the amendments made at the November 6,
2023 and February 5, 2024 commission meetings. The Community Services Commission
approved the workplan at the March 4, 2024 commission meeting.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.
 ANNUAL WORKPLAN 2024
The 2024 Workplan sets forth four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore.

  1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire Community
  a. Provide new programs for residents with the age groups, 13-18 and 30-50.
  b. Explore program offerings for persons with disabilities including but not
  limited to swim classes.
  c. Continue offering and expand the internship program for youth to assist
  with translation services.
  d. Serve as a liaison for events that City Council has requested be expanded or
  added. Commission members to provide feedback and support for these
  events.
  i. Staff to provide a layout/ general information to the commission for
  review. Commission to appoint two members to serve as a
  committee and work with staff.
  e. Commission to develop a youth ambassador program, host interviews and
  appoint two non-voting ambassadors to the commission.

  2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Commissioners to staff the Community Services Department information
  booth at City events.
  b. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San
  Gabriel area and various other neighborhoods such as a tiny tots
  soccer class at Marshall Park or a partnership with the Garvey School
  District.

  3. Embrace and Celebrate Community Diversity
  a. Partner and collaborate with various cultural and interfaith organizations to
  assist in the development and implementation of events and services
  i. Examples include: Partnering with the HEAR Commission, Native
  American Community and interfaith groups

  4. Develop Innovative Resources and Tools to Achieve our Mission
  a. Collect survey data with targeted questions to improve, enhance and seek
  additional services as needed
 b. Utilize social platforms to reach various audiences
  i. For example: Utilizing WeChat social media
c. Cross promote programs through various City Departments
  i. For example: utilize Police Department’s Neighborhood Watch to
  disseminate information.
d. Recommend that City Council approve the release of an RFP for a new
  registration software during fiscal year 2024/25.
e. Recommend that City Council approve the addition of a part time case
  manager through a third party provider.
